title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1965 notes on a 'Galois theory of motives'. T denotes the space of fibre functors, i.e. torsors under the motivic Galois group, and T_α a variant or component of it. The page enumerates which fibre-functor torsors a base X carries; case 2° is X dominated by Spec Z, i.e. X has points of residue characteristic 0.

(i) l-adic realisations. For every prime l there is a point ξ_l of T(Z_l): the l-adic étale fibre functor. It comes from an element of T_α over some l-adic object Z̃_{lZ} (reading uncertain). ξ_l depends on the choice of a geometric point x̄ of X. Changing x̄ changes it only up to the action of π_1, giving the relation between ξ_{x̄,l} and ξ_{x,l}. In modern terms, the étale realisations form a lisse l-adic system over X, i.e. a π_1-equivariant family of fibre functors.

(ii) p-adic realisations. If X has points of characteristic p > 0, one gets crystalline fibre functors ξ_{x,p} and an integral variant ξ^0_{x,p}. A comparison is then posed. Take y a point of characteristic p with values in a perfect field k, and x a point of characteristic 0 (implicitly specialising to y). The question is the relation between ξ_{y,p} (crystalline, over W(k)) and ξ_{x,p} ⊗_{Z_p} W(k) (p-adic étale, extended to W(k)). Grothendieck expects that they are 'in general not isomorphic, doubtless'. Heavily struck lines then suggest conditions or extensions under which they would nevertheless be isomorphic.

(iii) de Rham realisation. For a point x with values in a field k of characteristic 0, one has ξ_{x,∞} ∈ T_α(k) via Hodge–de Rham cohomology. The (two?) filtrations need not be built into the torsor. The vertical left margin seems to compare the role of the Hodge filtration in the de Rham fibre functor with the crystalline side.

The page is thus a sketch of the 'system of realisations' attached to a motive over an arithmetic base: étale for l ≠ p, crystalline at char-p points, de Rham at char-0 points, plus the specialisation and comparison maps among them. It also flags the p-adic étale versus crystalline comparison as non-trivial.

The paper is reused: the neighbouring pages are a Bourbaki Tribu 59 typescript on semisimple Lie algebras.
errors: The comparison in (ii) silently requires x to specialise to y; this is not stated.

Non-isomorphism as a mere torsor is not obvious. If k is algebraically closed, K = W(k)[1/p] has cohomological dimension ≤ 1, so torsors under a connected reductive group over K are trivial by Steinberg. The real obstruction is the absence of a canonical (Frobenius- and Galois-compatible) isomorphism, which later required period rings such as B_cris. The 'sans doute' is therefore correct only in a refined sense.
Notation ξ_{x,∞} for the de Rham realisation is a bit odd: ∞ usually indexes the Betti/Hodge realisation. The transcription and the image agree on ∞ here, though.

ideas.what: Motives over a base X give a compatible family of fibre functors: l-adic étale for all l, depending on a geometric point up to π_1
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian fibre functors / l-adic realisations as lisse sheaves; system of realisations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (motives); Deligne 1979–82 (absolute Hodge cycles), Jannsen, Deligne 1989 (systems of realisations)
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra's Catégories tannakiennes (1972) and Récoltes et Semailles; no direct publication of this list

ideas.what: Crystalline fibre functor at characteristic-p points, with an integral variant ξ^0_{x,p}
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968); letter to Tate 1966

ideas.what: Comparison of the crystalline realisation at y (char p) with the p-adic étale realisation at a char-0 lift x, tensored with W(k); expected not isomorphic in general
ideas.modern_name: p-adic comparison problem / Grothendieck's 'mysterious functor'; Fontaine's B_cris comparison
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (ICM 1970, mysterious functor); Fontaine, Fontaine–Messing, Faltings, Tsuji
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux, ICM Nice 1970

ideas.what: de Rham realisation at char-0 points via Hodge–de Rham, with filtration(s) considered as extra structure rather than part of the torsor
ideas.modern_name: de Rham fibre functor; Hodge filtration as extra structure (filtered fibre functor)
ideas.where_published: Saavedra Rivano, Catégories tannakiennes (1972), on graded and filtered fibre functors

missed.claim: Possibly early documentary evidence that Grothendieck formulated the p-adic étale/crystalline comparison as a comparison of motivic Galois torsors. This would be before the 1970 'mysterious functor' statement, if the 1965–66 date holds. He also explicitly expected non-isomorphism over W(k).
missed.quote: relation ... entre ξ_{y,p} et ξ_{x,p} ⊗_{Z_p} W(k) ... Ils ne sont en général pas isomorphes, sans doute.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for dating the origin of p-adic Hodge theory questions. Mathematically it is subsumed by Fontaine–Messing/Faltings and by torsor-comparison results for p-adic period torsors (e.g. Kisin, and work on G-crystals).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a sketch of the realisation torsors (ℓ-adic, crystalline, de Rham) for motives over an arithmetic base, all known later. The modestly notable point is an early, explicit framing of the crystalline versus p-adic étale comparison at the level of fibre-functor torsors. That predates the 1970 ICM formulation if the date is right, but the uncertain dating and the largely illegible struck passages limit its weight.
transcription_corrections: Heading reads '2°) X [est] dominé par Spec Z, i.e. X contient des pts de car. résiduelle nulle' — consistent.
In (i), '∀ ℓ ∈ P' (P = set of primes); the target looks like T_α(Z̃_{ℓZ}) or T_α(Z_ℓ-adic object) — uncertain.
Line after (i): likely 'ξ_ℓ dépend du choix d'un pt géom. quelconque de X, et est indép. à un choix près modulo opérations de π_1, relation ξ_{x̄,ℓ} ~ ξ_{x,ℓ}'.
In (ii): 'Si X a des points x de car. p>0, on a ... des ξ_{x,p}, ξ^0_{x,p}' — first gap possibly 'des fibrations cristallines' / 'dualisations' (uncertain).
In (iii): 'Si x est un pt à val. dans un corps k de car 0, on a ξ_{x,∞} ∈ T_α(k) par Hodge–de Rham. Il n'y a pas lieu de [tenir compte / munir] avec ses (2) filtrations'.
